subject: physics
title: Wavefront Run
summary: Keep the karts on the wave crests as light enters a medium, then turn a marching column with Huygens’ wavelets.
ncertRef: Section 10.3, Refraction and reflection of plane waves using Huygens principle
concepts: Speed of light in a medium
Refraction as a change of speed
Dispersion: speed in glass depends on colour
learningOutcome: The student can find the speed and wavelength of light in a medium from n, knows the frequency is unchanged, and uses Huygens’ construction to get sin r / sin i = v₂/v₁.

levels.title: Mud run
levels.adds: Baseline: in a medium of index n the speed is c/n and the wavelength λ/n, while the frequency stays the same (Ex 10.1, 10.3a; Example 10.1).
hints: The speed in the medium is v = c/n, with c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s.
The frequency cannot change, so v/λ′ = c/λ and λ′ = λ/n.
A test shot tells you whether your two numbers keep the frequency the same.

levels.title: The marching column
levels.adds: New idea: Huygens’ wavelets at the new speed bend the front, so sin r / sin i = v₂/v₁ (Section 10.3, Ex 10.2).
hints: The end of the front that reaches the ground first changes speed first.
sin r / sin i = v₂ / v₁ for a front entering the new ground.
Take the inverse sine in degrees and move the dial to the nearest half degree.

levels.title: Rainbow race
levels.adds: New: dispersion: violet is slower in glass than red, so a violet pulse needs a head start of d(n_v − n_r)/c to exit with the red one (Ex 10.3).
hints: In glass the speed is c/n.
Violet has the larger n, so it is the slower colour.
The extra time through thickness d is d(n_v − n_r)/c.

misconceptions: The frequency of light changes when it enters glass
Light slows down in glass because it loses energy
Reflected light has a different speed from the incident light
